A GOOD NEW YEAR
By MARY GEORGE M.B.E., Director, Electrical Association for Women
A "good new year" has many meanings, and in giving all our readers this time-honoured greeting I hope that it will have for each one of you just that interpretation that you would wish it to have—in your homes, in your careers, in your hobbies and in your entertainments. We have just left an old year full of new developments and promises to be fulfilled or furthered in 1960.

title: Chief
brief_context: An elderly chief in Lagos who spoke with Vera Stowell.
brief_extract:
In the towns
In the towns of Ghana and Nigeria, there is great interest in everything up-to-date and modern. In Lagos I talked with a chief who, having seen some of our equipment and talked about all the modern labour-saving devices, said with feeling, "I never thought I live to see this day". He was elderly, and I thought of the great changes which had taken place in Nigeria during his lifetime.

article_title: PAI NAA The Story of Nona Baker, M.B.E.
brief_extract:
(Constable, 18/-.)
Many E.A.W. members will have heard Miss Baker speak of her life in the Malayan jungle during the war, and will have realised what a world of difference divides the life she led as a white woman with a band of Chinese Communist guerillas fighting the Japanese and her present one as Branch Development Secretary of the E.A.W.! In this graphically told story are some of the details of many months of hardship, and imagination will supply those other details of suspense and tension which must have daily beset Pai Naa who, after her brother had died, did not know that her story would have a happy ending.

Margarine was invented in 1869 by a French
scientist named Mège Mouriés, who won the
prize offered by Napoleon III to anyone who,
from domestic supplies, could find a substitute
for butter. Mège Mouriés, had noticed that, even
if kept without food for a few days, cows still
produced milk with a fat content that could be
churned into butter, because they drew upon
their bodily reserves of fat, and he set himself
the task of discovering a means of reproducing
artificially what the cow carried out naturally.
